name: ps1-render
note: Read by eye. keep = how it is made (copied verbatim); replace is set per slide.
keep: KEEP — the making of the image, copy exactly:

· MEDIUM: a frame captured from a late-1990s PlayStation-1 real-time 3D game. Not concept art, not a modern render. Low internal resolution upscaled — everything is soft and slightly blurry, with visible pixel structure.
· GEOMETRY: aggressively low polygon count. Flat-shaded facets, visible triangle seams, hard angular silhouettes. Hair and foliage are FLAT INTERSECTING PLANES with alpha-cut edges, not strands.
· ARTEFACTS: at least one visible shading glitch — a hard dark triangle where the normals break. Texture seams misaligned at polygon edges. No cast shadows, no reflections, no ambient occlusion.
· TEXTURES: low-resolution blurry bitmaps stretched over the geometry, muddy detail.
· LIGHTING: flat vertex lighting, no falloff. Background light sources are simple bright emissive blobs and lit rectangles, blown out and bloomy.
· POST: heavy monochrome grain over everything, soft bloom on bright areas, dark vignette in the corners, CRT softness.
· COLOUR CAST: one sickly saturated hue floods the entire frame including the shadows.
· No readable text, no letters, no numerals, no logo, no watermark anywhere.
